page.layout: One text column, justified, with the running head "ad Lectorem." above it. No marginal notes, no page number, no catchword. The text runs on past the foot of the page.

main_text.p: cœperunt ab opusculo quod Theophrastus Erefius, cum ad incultos & male dolatos mores instituendos, auerruncandam è mentibus amentiam, tum ad virtutum & vitiorum indagădas naturas H᾽ΘIKOYS XAPAKTHPAS, quasi ἤθων ἀ-χονισμὸς inscripsit. Sed ut varia & incerta sunt aulicorum vices & sedes, quos plerumque improuisus negotiorum vortex alio abducit, cum ad coronidem vergeret opus, allati sunt regij codicilli, quibus Illust. de VIC in aulam euocatur, ad praeclaram legationem in Britanniam suscipiendum. Is Casaubonum optauit comitem, & ut non solet pendere ex crastino, aut ἐς ἄνεμον τὰ ἀσθ-ξαῖα reijcere, tam subitam profectionem repente adeo instituit, ut abeunti vix

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "VIC" (printed V1C; the figure may be a broken I, so [?] was not added in the text but should be checked). The Greek "H᾽ΘIKOYS" begins with a mark over the initial that may be a rough breathing; the Greek after "quasi" (ἤθων ἀ-χονισμὸς) and the Greek after "aut" (ἐς ἄνεμον τὰ ἀσθ-ξαῖα) are read from a small, soft scan and should be checked against the original. "cùm" is printed with a grave accent and is given as "cum". The word "vix" at the end stands alone on the last line, right-aligned, and is part of the running text, so it is not a catchword. Italic boundaries in the first sentence are uncertain.
